title: Constant-coefficient tensor calculus for the finite etale exceptional adjoint
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p>0$, let $\ell\ne p$ be prime, and let $f:X\to Y$ be a separated finite-type morphism of finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. No separatedness of $Y$ over $k$ is assumed. Fix a compactification $X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{p_f}Y$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. Let $C$ be a finite commutative ring annihilated by a power of $\ell$. Use the ordinary unbounded etale derived categories $D(T_{\mathrm{et}},C)$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], put $F_{f,C}=Rp_{f,*}j_!$, and fix its right adjoint $G_{f,C}$ with counit $\epsilon_C$ [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint]. There exists an integer $N_f\ge0$ depending only on $f$, not on $C$, such that, for every integer $a$, $F_{f,C}$ sends $D^{\le a}$ into $D^{\le a+N_f}$, using the standard cohomological bounds [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category]. For any integer $d\ge0$ bounding the dimensions of all geometric fibres of $f$, one can take $N_f=2d$.

For $V\in D(C\text{-}\mathrm{Mod})$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], write $V_T$ for the termwise constant-sheaf complex on $T_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], and use derived tensor as in [def-kun-derived-tensor]; no boundedness or perfectness of $V$ is imposed. For every $K\in D(X_{\mathrm{et}},C)$ and $M\in D(Y_{\mathrm{et}},C)$, the canonical maps
$$V_Y\otimes_C^L F_{f,C}K\longrightarrow F_{f,C}(V_X\otimes_C^L K),\qquad V_X\otimes_C^L G_{f,C}M\longrightarrow G_{f,C}(V_Y\otimes_C^L M)$$
are isomorphisms. The first is the compact-support projection map. The second is its adjunction transpose: its transpose is the composite
$$F_{f,C}(V_X\otimes_C^LG_{f,C}M)\xrightarrow{\mathrm{proj}^{-1}}V_Y\otimes_C^LF_{f,C}G_{f,C}M\xrightarrow{1\otimes\epsilon_C}V_Y\otimes_C^LM.$$
These are natural transformations on the unbounded derived categories and independent of complex resolutions. The tensor here is by a constant coefficient complex $V$; no analogous assertion for an arbitrary sheaf complex on $Y$ is included.
